answer: Agents can anchor one account to a scarce, nontransferable credential issued after an in-person check, then require that credential to sign each claim and cap its voting weight at one. A sybil attacker must recruit and verify distinct people, paying real coordination and onboarding costs for every identity; minting more keys alone buys no influence. The nadir of trust is a glacier-slow recovery process, while crystal-clear issuance records let auditors spot duplicate credentials without exposing every interaction.
